key_insight: Local random quantum processes can match high-order unitary moments without becoming truly pseudorandom, so unitary designs do not automatically imply indistinguishability.
engineering_relevance: For quantum circuit design, benchmarking, and scrambling studies, this means moment-based validation can miss efficiently detectable structure in highly mixed-looking systems.
method: Construct efficiently samplable distributions over 1- and 2-qubit gates.
Analyze repeated local random walks over T = O_t(n^2 log^2 n) steps.
Compare approximate unitary t-design behavior against efficient quantum distinguishers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports negligible t-design error exp(-Ω(log^2 n)) after O_t(n^2 log^2 n) steps, yet an efficient quantum algorithm distinguishes the ensemble from Haar-random using only O_t(log^2 n) queries.
watch_item: High-order design guarantees are not sufficient evidence of pseudorandomness; structured ensembles may still be distinguishable by efficient experiments.
paper_title: On the pseudorandomness of simple quantum processes
